## 0. Premise re-verification — the card's two instruments, re-read at head

Both instruments still point the same way, and the headline holds: **all 17 methods have no published response contract bound to their route.** Four sub-premises do not survive contact with head, and three of them change what closing this card costs.

### 0.1 VERIFIED — every ledger row still reports `responseSchema=None`

Re-derived by parsing the ledger sources directly (the resolver's own rule: a row declares a response only if it carries a `responseSchema` key naming a live `@objectstack/spec/api` export).

| ledger | rows for these 17 | any `responseSchema` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts` | 11 (L302, 306-309, 311-313, 352-354) | **none** |
| `packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts` | 9 (L146-148, 151-152, 180, 183-184, 200) | **none** |

### 0.2 CORRECTION 1 — it is 20 ledger rows, not 17, because three routes are DUAL-MOUNTED

The card tags each route with one surface. Three carry a row in **both** ledgers, because both surfaces mount them:

| client method | runtime row | rest row |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `meta.getPublished` | `route-ledger.ts:352` | `rest-route-ledger.ts:200` |
| `meta.listDrafts` | `route-ledger.ts:353` | `rest-route-ledger.ts:147` |
| `meta.migrateStored` | `route-ledger.ts:354` | `rest-route-ledger.ts:148` |

This is load-bearing for whoever implements, because **the two surfaces answer different envelopes** (section 8.1), and a filled row is a per-surface claim.

### 0.3 CORRECTION 2 — `meta.migrateStored` is NOT missing a ledger row

The card's table says `meta.migrateStored  NO LEDGER ROW`. It has two (above), both `responseSchema=None`. The route is `POST /meta/_migrate-stored`, ledgered `disposition: 'sdk', client: 'meta.migrateStored'` on both surfaces. Nothing to add to a ledger here — only a schema to name.

### 0.4 CORRECTION 3 — "the producers themselves are untyped" is FALSE at head

This is the sub-premise that changes the shape of the work. The card says of the eight `packages.*` handlers: *"they reach the protocol service through an `any` cast, so there is no declared type anywhere on the path to lift."*

The cast is real. The second clause is not. **Every producer behind those casts carries a complete, concrete, inline-declared return type** — the `as any` at the call site erases a type that exists a few files away, precisely and in full:

| handler call site (`runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`) | producer | declared return |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L687 `discardPackageDrafts` | `metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:16615` | `success, discardedCount, failedCount, discarded[type,name], failed[type,name,error,code?]` |
| L710 `listCommits` | `protocol.ts:17593` | array of `id, operation('apply'/'revert'), message?, actor?, aiModel?, parentCommitId?, itemCount, items[type,name,existedBefore,prevVersion], createdAt?` |
| L732 `revertCommit` | `protocol.ts:17703` | `success, revertedCount, failedCount, reverted[type,name,action('removed'/'restored')], failed[...], revertCommitId?` |
| L756 `rollbackToPackageCommit` | `protocol.ts:18206` | `success, revertedCommits[string], failed[commitId,error]` |
| L805 `reassignOrphanedMetadata` | `protocol.ts:17325` | `success, reassignedCount, reassigned[type,name], targetPackageId` |
| L832 `duplicatePackage` | `protocol.ts:16971` | `success, copiedCount, failedCount, targetPackageId, copied[type,name], failed[type,name,error]` |

The same holds for the `meta.*` side: `getMetaDiagnostics` (`protocol.ts:5423`), `listDrafts` (`:15480`), `findReferencesToMeta` (`:19668`), `auditMetaItem` (`:7089`), `rollbackMetaItem` (`:18289`), `diffMetaItem` (`:18523`) all declare their full return inline. `auditMetaItem` is not even reached through a cast — the REST handler calls `p.auditMetaItem(...)` on the typed interface (`rest-server.ts:6088`).

**What this changes.** The card's own framing — a *missing contract*, not a missing annotation — was derived from "nothing declared to lift". The accurate statement at head is narrower and cheaper: the shapes are **declared and stable, in the wrong package for the client to reach**. `packages/client` depends on `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/spec` only; the declarations live in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`. So for most of the 17 the work is *transcribe a known shape into a spec schema*, not *invent one from handler reading*. That is what makes a large DESCRIBE-ONLY bucket possible at all (section 7).

### 0.5 CORRECTION 4 — the card's evidence line for `packages.publish` names the wrong handler

The card lists `domains/packages.ts:660  (protocol as any).publishPackageDrafts` as `packages.publish`'s producer. `publishPackageDrafts` is the producer for `POST /packages/:id/publish-drafts`, which is `packages.publishDrafts` — a **different method, already bound** to `PublishPackageDraftsResponse` since #9406 and explicitly not one of the 17 (`client/src/index.ts:1651`).

`packages.publish` (`POST /packages/:id/publish`) does not touch the protocol service at all. Its handler (`domains/packages.ts:353-363`) resolves the **metadata service** and calls `(metadataService as any).publishPackage(id, body)`. So the card's count of "8 handlers calling `(protocol as any)`" is 7; the eighth method reaches a different service — and, as section 5.3 records, one whose result type is already published in `@objectstack/spec`.

**`premise_still_valid: true`** — the card's question is real, its headline reading is correct, all 17 are genuinely unbound. The four corrections change the cost and the routing, not whether the card should exist.

---

## 1. Population — the 17, with their producers and emissions

Emission column: `success(x)` is the dispatcher envelope `{ success: true, data: x }` (`runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts:367`); `res.json(x)` is the REST server answering `x` bare.

### 1a. The nine `meta.*`

| # | client method | route | producer | emission |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `meta.getPublished` | GET `/meta/:type/:name/published` | `getMetaItemLayered(...).overlay`, else legacy `getPublished` | `success(overlay)` / `res.json(data)` |
| 2 | `meta.listDrafts` | GET `/meta/_drafts` | `protocol.listDrafts` | `success(result)` / `res.json(result)` |
| 3 | `meta.migrateStored` | POST `/meta/_migrate-stored` | `protocol.migrateStoredMetadata` | `success(report)` / `res.json(report)` |
| 4 | `meta.getDiagnostics` | GET `/meta/diagnostics` | `protocol.getMetaDiagnostics` | `res.json(result)` |
| 5 | `meta.getReferences` | GET `/meta/:type/:name/references` | `protocol.findReferencesToMeta` | `res.json(result)` |
| 6 | `meta.getBookTree` | GET `/meta/book/:name/tree` | `resolveBookTree(...)` from `@objectstack/spec/system` | `res.json(tree)` |
| 7 | `meta.getAudit` | GET `/meta/:type/:name/audit` | `protocol.auditMetaItem` (typed call, no cast) | `res.json(result)` |
| 8 | `meta.rollbackItem` | POST `/meta/:type/:name/rollback` | `protocol.rollbackMetaItem` | `res.json(result)` |
| 9 | `meta.diffItem` | GET `/meta/:type/:name/diff` | `protocol.diffMetaItem` | `res.json(result)` |

### 1b. The eight `packages.*`

All eight are served by the runtime dispatcher only — **`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` mounts no twin for any of them**, so each has exactly one surface and one envelope. Verified by grep for each path in the REST server: zero hits.

| # | client method | route | producer | emission |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | `packages.publish` | POST `/packages/:id/publish` | `metadataService.publishPackage` yielding `PackagePublishResult` | `success(result)` |
| 11 | `packages.discardDrafts` | POST `/packages/:id/discard-drafts` | `protocol.discardPackageDrafts` | `success(result)` |
| 12 | `packages.listCommits` | GET `/packages/:id/commits` | `protocol.listCommits` (returns a bare ARRAY) | `success({ commits })` |
| 13 | `packages.revertCommit` | POST `/packages/:id/commits/:commitId/revert` | `protocol.revertCommit` | `success(result)` |
| 14 | `packages.rollback` | POST `/packages/:id/rollback` | `protocol.rollbackToPackageCommit` | `success(result)` |
| 15 | `packages.export` | GET `/packages/:id/export` | local `assemblePackageManifest`, a Record of string to any | `success(manifest)` |
| 16 | `packages.adoptOrphans` | POST `/packages/:id/adopt-orphans` | `protocol.reassignOrphanedMetadata` | `success(result)` |
| 17 | `packages.duplicate` | POST `/packages/:id/duplicate` | `protocol.duplicatePackage` | `success(result)` |

**Where the shape is incidental rather than stable.** Only three:

- **#12 `listCommits`** — the producer returns a bare array; the `{ commits }` wrapper is minted **at the handler** (`packages.ts:713`), nowhere else. The array element shape is stable; the wrapper is a handler-local choice with no declaration behind it.
- **#15 `export`** — `assemblePackageManifest` (`packages.ts:1016`) declares a Record of string to any (or null) and builds its keys **dynamically from the metadata type registry**: `manifest[plural] = items.map(clean)` per type present, plus fixed `id`, `name`, `version` and optional `label`. The key set is open by construction; only the four fixed keys are pinnable.
- **#1 `getPublished`** — answers a metadata **item body**, i.e. the union of every metadata type's shape. The layered producer that feeds it declares that field as `z.unknown()` on purpose (`spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts:489`, "LAYER 2 — the stored customization row ALONE").

Everything else is a fixed, fully-declared record.

---

## 2. Consumer census, with controls

Method: `grep -rn` for `meta.METHOD(` / `packages.METHOD(` over `*.ts *.tsx *.mts *.js *.mjs *.md *.mdx` across each repo, `node_modules` and `CHANGELOG.md` excluded; plus a separate URL sweep for direct REST callers of each route path.

### 2a. SDK call sites

| client method | objectstack | objectui | cloud |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `meta.getPublished` | 2 (both tests) | 0 | 0 |
| `meta.listDrafts` | 2 (both tests) | 0 | 0 |
| `meta.migrateStored` | 3 (**all docs**, 0 tests) | 0 | 0 |
| `meta.getDiagnostics` | 3 (2 tests, 1 doc) | 0 | 0 |
| `meta.getReferences` | 2 (1 test, 1 doc) | 0 | 0 |
| `meta.getBookTree` | 2 (1 test, 1 doc) | 0 | 0 |
| `meta.getAudit` | 2 (1 test, 1 doc) | 0 | 0 |
| `meta.rollbackItem` | 2 (1 test, 1 doc) | 0 | 0 |
| `meta.diffItem` | 2 (1 test, 1 doc) | 0 | 0 |
| `packages.publish` | 1 test (+1 FALSE POSITIVE, below) | 0 | 0 |
| `packages.discardDrafts` | 1 test | 0 | 0 |
| `packages.listCommits` | 1 test | 0 | 0 |
| `packages.revertCommit` | 1 test | 0 | 0 |
| `packages.rollback` | 1 test | 0 | 0 |
| `packages.export` | 1 test | 0 | 0 |
| `packages.adoptOrphans` | 1 test | 0 | 0 |
| `packages.duplicate` | 1 test | 0 | 0 |

**Non-test, non-doc SDK call sites, all 17, all three repos: ZERO.**

**One false positive, discarded rather than counted.** `packages/services/service-package/README.md:39` matches `packages.publish(` but is the kernel `PackageService` — `kernel.getService('package').publish({ manifest, metadata })`, a different object with a different arity. Not a `client.packages` call.

### 2b. Controls — the same sweep, same patterns, neighbouring methods

The zeros above are about these methods, not about the sweep.

| control | objectstack | objectui | cloud |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `meta.getItem(` | 22 | 9 | 0 |
| `meta.saveItem(` | 39 | **37** | 0 |
| `meta.publishItem(` | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| `packages.list(` | 10 | 0 | **9** |
| `packages.publishDrafts(` | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| `packages.install(` | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| `data.create(` | 18 | 0 | 0 |

Each repo has at least one control in high double digits — objectui at 37 `saveItem`, cloud at 9 `packages.list`, objectstack at 39/22/18. The sweep finds real sites in all three.

### 2c. Direct REST callers — this is where the real consumers are

The SDK is not how these routes are reached in production. The client's own docblock says so (*"Studio reached them via raw fetch"*), and the sweep confirms it. **objectui has live consumers of eight of the 17 routes**; cloud has one.

| repo | file:line | route | one of the 17? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| objectui | `app-shell/src/preview/usePendingDrafts.ts:48` | GET `/meta/_drafts` | **yes — #2** |
| objectui | `app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PackagesPage.tsx:293,364,415` | GET `/meta/_drafts` | **yes — #2** |
| objectui | `app-shell/src/preview/commitHistory.ts:160` | GET `/packages/:id/commits` | **yes — #12** |
| objectui | `app-shell/src/preview/commitHistory.ts:195` | POST `/packages/:id/commits/:commitId/revert` | **yes — #13** |
| objectui | `app-shell/src/views/studio-design/packages-io.ts:64` | POST `/packages/:id/duplicate` | **yes — #17** |
| objectui | `data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts` (`diagnostics`/`audit`/`rollback`/`diff`) | 4 of the meta routes | **yes — #4, #7, #8, #9** |
| objectui | `metadata-admin/previews/BookPreview.tsx:149` | GET `/meta/book/:name/tree` | **yes — #6** (link only) |
| cloud | `scripts/eval/golden-prompts.mjs:203,277,351` | GET `/meta/_drafts` | **yes — #2** |
| objectui | `StudioDesignSurface.tsx:554`, `usePublishAllDrafts.ts:77`, `PendingDraftsBar.tsx:77`, `AiChatPage.tsx:2298` | POST `/packages/:id/publish-drafts` | no — control; that method IS bound |

The last row is a second, sharper control: the one `packages.*` lifecycle route that already has a published schema is also the one objectui calls most (4 sites). The sweep is not blind to this family.

**Not reached from anywhere, in any repo, by SDK or by URL:** `meta.getPublished`, `meta.migrateStored`, `meta.getReferences`, `packages.publish`, `packages.discardDrafts`, `packages.rollback`, `packages.export`, `packages.adoptOrphans` — 8 of the 17 have zero consumers of any kind outside objectstack's own tests and docs.

---

## 3. Per call site — what the RESPONSE is actually used for

### 3a. objectstack's own SDK call sites: all but two discard the response

Every one of the 9 `meta.*` test sites (`client/src/client.test.ts:262-322`, `meta-automation-descriptors.test.ts:28-60`) asserts **only** on the request — URL, method, body. Not one reads a field back.

The `packages.*` suite (`client/src/packages-lifecycle.test.ts`) reads exactly two fields across eight methods:

| method | field read | rest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `listCommits` | `out.commits` (length) | — |
| `export` | `manifest.id` | — |
| `publish`, `discardDrafts`, `revertCommit`, `rollback`, `adoptOrphans`, `duplicate` | none | response discarded |

**Fields re-read across all 17 SDK call sites: 2. Persisted: 0.**

Contrast from the same files, showing these suites do read responses when a shape is being pinned: `meta.getLegalNextStates` asserts `out.object` / `out.field` / `out.next`; `packages.update` and `packages.list` assert their bound shapes.

### 3b. FIDELITY WARNING — 4 of the 9 `meta.*` test mocks contradict the real producer

Because nothing reads the response, nothing has ever checked that the mocked body resembles what the route answers. Measured, mock against producer:

| method | mocked body | producer actually answers | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `getDiagnostics` | `{ items: [] }` | `entries, total, scannedTypes, scannedItems, stats` | **no `items` key exists** |
| `getBookTree` | `{ tree: [] }` | `ResolvedBook` = `name, label?, groups[]` | **no `tree` key exists** |
| `rollbackItem` | `{ restored: true }` | `success, version, seq, restoredFromVersion, message?` | **no `restored` key exists** |
| `diffItem` | `{ changes: [] }` | `type, name, fromVersion, toVersion, added, removed, changed` | **no `changes` key exists** |
| `getReferences` | `{ references: [] }` | `{ references: [...] }` | matches |
| `getAudit` | `{ events: [] }` | `{ events: [...] }` | matches |
| `listDrafts` | `{ drafts: [] }` | `{ drafts: [...] }` | matches |
| `getPublished` | `{ name: 'all_leads' }` | an arbitrary metadata item body | plausible |
| `migrateStored` | (no SDK test) | `StoredMigrationReport` | — |

Four invented shapes sit in the repo's own test file, green, indistinguishable from measurements. They are not evidence of anything about the routes, and they are the concrete cost of an unbound surface. **Whoever authors the schemas should treat these four mocks as needing replacement, not as a starting point.**

### 3c. objectui's live consumers — what they read, and the tolerance chains

| consumer | route | fields read | envelope handling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `commitHistory.ts:159-191` `fetchCommits` | #12 | `id, operation, message, actor, aiModel, itemCount, createdAt` — **7 of 9**; skips `parentCommitId`, `items` | **THREE-arm chain**: bare array, or `{commits}`, or `{data:{commits}}` |
| `commitHistory.ts:193-208` `revertCommit` | #13 | `success` only | **TWO-arm chain**: `payload.data` then `payload` |
| `usePendingDrafts.ts:44-65` `fetchPendingDrafts` | #2 | `type, name, packageId` — **3 of 6**; skips `organizationId`, `updatedAt`, `updatedBy` | **THREE-arm chain**: bare array, `{drafts}`, `{data:{drafts}}` |
| `packages-io.ts:63-76` `duplicatePackage` | #17 | `success` at TOP level | **no unwrap — this is a defect, section 9** |
| `metadata-client.ts` + `useMetadata.ts:250-370` + `DiagnosticsPage.tsx` | #4 | `entries[].type/.name/.diagnostics`, `total`, `scannedItems`, `scannedTypes`, `stats[].count/.locked/.packages` — **all 6 top-level fields, fully consumed** | direct |
| `AuditPanel.tsx:125-260` | #7 | `events[]` then `id, occurredAt, actor, operation, outcome, lockState, lockOverridden, note, code` — **9 of 11** | direct |
| `BookPreview.tsx:149` | #6 | **none** — renders an anchor link to the route for a human to open | n/a |
| `metadata-client.ts:1189/1221` `rollback` / `diff` | #8, #9 | typed as a caller-supplied generic; docblocks name `{ success, version, seq, restoredFromVersion, message }` and `{ added, removed, changed }` | direct |
| cloud `golden-prompts.mjs:203,277,351` | #2 | reads the draft list to count/assert pending drafts in an eval harness | direct |

**The three multi-arm chains are the measured cost of contract absence, and they are exactly the shape the contract-first rule names** (a consumer widening because the producer declares nothing). Only ONE arm of each is live: `/packages/:id/commits` and `/meta/_drafts` are both served with the dispatcher envelope, so `{data:{commits}}` / `{data:{drafts}}` is the real one and the other two arms have never fired. They are speculation preserved in production code because nothing said which was true.

### 3d. objectui has independently re-declared three of these shapes — and they AGREE with the producer

The strongest single piece of evidence in this survey. Written in a different repo by different hands, against no published schema:

| objectui declaration | objectstack producer | agreement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MetadataDiagnosticsSummary` (`metadata-client.ts:481-500`) — `entries, total, scannedTypes, scannedItems, stats` | `getMetaDiagnostics` (`protocol.ts:5423`) | **exact**, one delta: objectui marks `stats` and `stats[].locked` OPTIONAL, with the comment *"Optional for backward compatibility with older framework versions that do not yet emit it"*. The producer declares both required. |
| `MetadataAuditEntry` + `MetadataAuditResponse` (`metadata-client.ts:418-448`) — 11 fields | `auditMetaItem` (`protocol.ts:7089`) | **exact — field for field, nullability for nullability, both closed enums identical** |
| `rollback` docblock `{ success, version, seq, restoredFromVersion, message }` | `rollbackMetaItem` (`protocol.ts:18289`) | **exact** |

Two independent authors converging on the same shape is the best available evidence that the shape is stable and describable without a ruling.

---

## 4. Tests pinning a response shape: near-zero

Systematic search across `packages/client/src`, `packages/runtime/src/domains`, `packages/rest/src`, `packages/qa` (incl. `dogfood/`) for assertions on a response body of any of the 17 routes.

- **`return-type-precision.test.ts`** — the #11925 compile-time pin file. None of the 17 appear in it as a binding; one appears as a **negative** guard (section 5).
- **`packages-lifecycle.test.ts`** — two field reads, listed in 3a.
- **`client.test.ts` / `meta-automation-descriptors.test.ts`** — zero field reads, four wrong mocks.
- **`spec/src/api/protocol.test.ts:1857-1910`** — the one real shape suite touching any of the 17: it parses a *"verbatim-shaped capture of a real `auditMetaItem` return"* through `AuditMetaItemResponseSchema`, asserts member preservation, asserts the honest-empty `{events: []}` body parses, and asserts both enums stay closed. **Shaped from a real return, but handwritten — it has never seen a route response.** Under #3877's Stage-D rule that is coverage-shaped, not route conformance.
- **Docs** — `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx:229-240` shows 8 of the 9 `meta.*` methods being called; every example assigns the result and none reads a field off it. No published example commits to a shape.

**Response-shape dependents anywhere in objectstack: effectively zero.** The dependents are all in objectui (section 3c), and they read the *producer's* shape, not any declared one.

---

## 5. The card's near-miss, verified on current main — and it is WORSE than the card records

### 5.1 The card's ⭐ `PackageRollbackResponse` reading is CONFIRMED at head

`packages/spec/src/api/package-api.zod.ts:331-337`:

```
export const PackageRollbackResponseSchema = lazySchema(() => BaseResponseSchema.extend({
  data: z.object({
    success: z.boolean().describe('Whether the rollback succeeded'),
    restoredVersion: z.string().optional().describe('Restored version'),
    message: z.string().optional().describe('Rollback status message'),
  }),
}).describe('Rollback package response'));
```

versus what `client.packages.rollback(id, commitId, opts)` actually reaches — `rollbackToPackageCommit` (`protocol.ts:18206`), answering `success, revertedCommits (string array), failed[{commitId, error}]`. A *version* rollback declaration against a *commit* rollback operation. Binding it would compile and be false, exactly as the card says.

The #11925 guard is present and intact: `packages/client/src/return-type-precision.test.ts:307-311`, `declare const versionRollbackPayload: PackageRollbackResponse['data'];` with a `ts-expect-error` on `.commitId`. It is documented there as *"GREEN IN BOTH STATES — regression guards"*, alongside a second near-miss guard for `Environment` / `client.projects.*`.

### 5.2 The escalation the card did not record: the spec BINDS that schema to that exact live path

`package-api.zod.ts:398-441` declares `PackageApiContracts`, documented as *"Standard Package API contracts map. Used for generating SDKs, documentation, and route registration."* Its `rollbackPackage` entry:

```
rollbackPackage: {
  method: 'POST' as const,
  path: '/api/v1/packages/:packageId/rollback',
  input: PackageRollbackRequestSchema,
  output: PackageRollbackResponseSchema,
},
```

That path **is** the live route — `POST /packages/:id/rollback` mounted under `/api/v1`, differing only in the param's name. So `PackageRollbackResponse` is not merely "one import away and tempting". **The spec already declares an output for that route, and the declaration is false about it.** This is #12206's section-0 finding repeating in this family: a published declaration that outran the implementation, sitting where a future sweep will read it as authoritative.

## 8. Cross-cutting facts the implementing dispatch inherits

### 8.1 The three dual-mounted `meta.*` routes answer TWO different envelopes

`meta.getPublished`, `meta.listDrafts`, `meta.migrateStored` are mounted on both surfaces. The dispatcher wraps (`{ success: true, data: x }`); the REST server answers bare (`res.json(x)`). The SDK cannot tell, because `unwrapResponse` (`client/src/index.ts:5310-5318`) unwraps only when the body has BOTH a boolean `success` and a `data` key, and passes everything else through. So one client-side type is true on both surfaces — but the **ledger rows are per-surface and there are six of them**, and a `responseSchema` naming an enveloped shape would be false on the REST row (and vice versa). Whatever is authored must state which layer it describes.

### 8.2 A latent mis-unwrap hazard, worth a pin when the schemas land

`unwrapResponse`'s heuristic mis-fires on any **bare** payload that itself carries a boolean `success` AND a `data` key. None of the 17 producers does today — the closest are `rollbackMetaItem`, `discardPackageDrafts`, `duplicatePackage`, `reassignOrphanedMetadata`, `revertCommit`, `rollbackToPackageCommit` and `PackagePublishResult`, which all carry `success` but none of which carries `data`. Adding a `data` key to any of them later would silently change what the SDK returns. Cheap to pin alongside the schemas; invisible otherwise.

### 8.3 #3877's do-not-fill-without-conformance rule bites unevenly here

The only route with a schema (`meta.getAudit`) has parse coverage over a **handwritten** capture, not over a route response. Every describe-only candidate in bucket (a) will need conformance coverage authored fresh — and section 3b shows the existing test mocks cannot be reused for it, since four of them describe shapes that do not exist. Budget the conformance half as new work, not as adaptation.

### 8.4 Nothing in bucket (a) is a behaviour change

Every describe-only candidate transcribes a shape the producer already declares and already emits. Unlike #12206's fork, no option in bucket (a) alters a single byte on the wire; the only consumers that exist (section 3c) read fields the schemas would declare. The behaviour questions are confined to bucket (b), and even there only #15 and #1 touch what is emitted.

## 9. Out-of-scope finding, filed

**objectui#6593** — `duplicatePackage` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/packages-io.ts:64`) reads `success` at the **top level** of the response, which on this route is always the dispatcher envelope's `success: true`. The operation's own verdict is `data.success`, computed as `failed.length === 0 && copied.length > 0`.
